pages.ja:
抜けるような青空の下、朝一番で豆腐屋にて買い物をする。
テーブルに置かれた三百円で絹ごし豆腐を三丁購入し、
「お、士郎くん日曜だってのに偉いねえ！」
豆腐屋の二代目がサービスでくれた豆乳パックを飲みながら帰還する。

pages.en:
Beneath a blue sky clear enough to see forever, I make the tofu shop my first stop of the morning.

I use the three hundred yen left on the table to buy three blocks of silken tofu.

“Well, if it isn't Shirou! Running errands even on a Sunday? Good for you!”

On my way home, I drink the carton of soy milk the shop's second-generation owner gave me on the house.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I head to the tofu shop under the clear blue sky.
I buy three tofu with the 300 yen that was on the table.
“Oh, Shirou-kun. Great for you to come even on a Sunday!”
I go home drinking the soy milk I got as a service from the tofu shop owner.

pages.ja:
「
うん、満たされてる」
完璧だ。
シチュエーション的に、文句のつけどころのない気持ちいい朝である。
pages.jaRuby:
「
うん、満たされてる」
完璧だ。
シチュエーション的に、文句のつけどころのない気持ちいい朝である。
pages.en:
“——Yeah. This is the life.”

Perfect.

Given the circumstances, there is nothing whatsoever to criticize about this delightful morning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Yeah, this is great.”
This is perfect.
This is a perfect morning with nothing to complain about.

pages.ja:
「……なんだけど、なんか損したような……？」
はて、と首をかしげながら青空を仰ぐ。
大きめに切ってもらった豆腐、六十円の豆乳パック。
この幸せに匹敵するモノなんて、そう簡単には転がっていないと思うんだが。
pages.jaRuby:
「……なんだけど、なんか損したような……？」
はて、と首をかしげながら青空を仰ぐ。
大きめに切ってもらった豆腐、六十円の豆乳パック。
この幸せに匹敵するモノなんて、そう簡単には転がっていないと思うんだが。
pages.en:
“…Except I can't shake the feeling I've missed out on something…?”

Puzzled, I tilt my head back toward the blue sky.

Three generously cut blocks of tofu. A carton of soy milk worth sixty yen.

I can't imagine happiness to rival this simply lying around everywhere.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…But I feel like I’m at a loss…”
I tilt my head in wonder and look up at the sky.
A big serving of tofu and a 60-yen soy milk.
I don’t think good things like this happen that often.

pages.ja:
散歩がてらにゆっくりと戻ってきて、豆腐をどう使うか悩むコト二十分。
気が付けば時計の針は八時半を指していた。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
I take my time walking home, then spend twenty minutes deciding what to do with the tofu.

By the time I look up, the clock reads half past eight.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I slowly walked back and pondered what to do with the tofu for about twenty minutes.
It’s eight-thirty already.

pages.ja: 「おはようございます、シロウ。今朝は随分とゆっくりなのですね」
pages.jaRuby: 「おはようございます、シロウ。今朝は随分とゆっくりなのですね」
pages.en: “Good morning, Shirou. You are taking things unusually slowly today.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Good morning, Shirou. You are at ease this morning.”

pages.ja:
「ん？ ああ、おはようセイバー。今日は日曜で学校がないから、その分ゆっくりしていられるんだ。体の調子もいいから、朝飯が終わったら道場に行こう」
「ええ、望むところです。ではシロウ、半身の麻痺は完治したのですね」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Hm? Oh, good morning, Saber. It's Sunday, so there isn't any school. That gives us time to relax. I'm feeling good too, so let's go to the dojo after breakfast.”

“Gladly. Then the paralysis in half your body has healed completely, Shirou?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm? Oh, morning, Saber. I can relax since it’s Sunday and there’s no school today. I feel good, so let’s go to the dojo after breakfast.”
“Yes, that will be great. So your numbness has healed?”

pages.ja:
「あ、そう言えばそうだった。
商店街から気持ちよく散歩できたし、もうほとんど治ってるみたいだ。……ま、まだかすかに重いけど、この分なら明日には治ってる」
pages.jaRuby:
「あ、そう言えばそうだった。
商店街から気持ちよく散歩できたし、もうほとんど治ってるみたいだ。……ま、まだかすかに重いけど、この分なら明日には治ってる」
pages.en:
“Oh, right. That.

“I had a pleasant walk back from the shopping district, so it seems almost completely healed. …That side still feels faintly heavy, but at this rate I'll be fine tomorrow.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, you’re right.
I was able to walk from the shopping district without a problem, so I guess it’s pretty much healed. …It’s a bit heavy, but it should be fully healed by tomorrow.”

pages.ja: 「それは良かった。貴方が傷を負ったままでは私も立つ瀬がない。シロウがいつも通り厨房に立っていると、私も安心できます」
pages.jaRuby: 「それは良かった。[ruby text=マスター char=2]貴方が傷を負ったままでは私も立つ瀬がない。シロウがいつも通り厨房に立っていると、私も安心できます」
pages.en: “That is welcome news. I could hardly hold my head high while you—my Master—remained injured. Seeing Shirou at work in the kitchen as usual reassures me as well.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “That is good. I cannot be at ease if my Master is wounded. I can relax if I see you in the kitchen like always.”

pages.ja:
セイバーはテーブルの横、自分の定位置に腰を下ろす。
藤ねえと遠坂が起きてこないのは寝坊と言わざるを得ないが、休日なんだし、朝食が出来るまで寝かしておいてやろう。

pages.en:
Saber sits in her customary place beside the table.

There is no other word for Fuji and Tohsaka's failure to appear but oversleeping. Still, it is a holiday. I may as well let them sleep until breakfast is ready.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Saber takes a seat in her usual position beside the table.
Fuji-nee and Tohsaka are sleeping, but since it’s Sunday, I should let them sleep in until breakfast’s ready.

pages.ja:
「おはよう凛。昨夜はゆっくり眠れたようですね」
お。
なんて言ってる間に、遠坂が起きてきたみたいだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「おはよう凛。昨夜はゆっくり眠れたようですね」

“Good morning, Rin. It appears you slept well last night.”

Oh.

Speak of the devil. It sounds as though Tohsaka has finally woken up.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Good morning, Rin. It seems you were able to sleep well last night.”
Oh.
It seems Tohsaka’s awake.

pages.ja:
「……おはよ。別にそうでもなかったんだけどね。陽射しは眩しいし、零時過ぎてもごそごそやってるヤツラはいたし」
セイバーに答えながら、遠坂は居間に入ってくる。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Morning. Not particularly. The sunlight was dazzling, and certain people kept rustling around after midnight.”

Tohsaka answers Saber as she enters the living room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Morning. It wasn’t really like that. The light was bright and there were people moving about even past midnight.”
…Tohsaka answers Saber as she goes into the living room.

pages.ja:
さて。
朝から小言なんて言いたくないが、食パンを全滅させた理由ぐらいは問いたださねば。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
——Now, then.

I dislike beginning the morning with a lecture, but I will at least have to ask what happened to our entire supply of bread.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Well.
I don’t want to complain so early in the morning, but I have to know why she took all of the bread.

“Ah——uh.”

My pulse abruptly begins to pound.

…It must be that vivid red outfit.

The sight of it is so painful that whatever I meant to say has been kicked clean out of my head.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ah
um…”
My heart starts beating rapidly.
…It’s because of the red clothes.
It hurts my eyes so much that everything I wanted to say escapes my mind.

But——

But.

Tohsaka glares at me as though breakfast can wait.

“Why are you so slow? We’re going out today, so get ready quickly.”
